findings.description: The 1,800-square-foot storefront at 301 Union Street is legally two separate units — part zoned commercial, about two-thirds zoned residential — despite having been run as one combined commercial space for decades, including by a celebrated grocery, Speedy's Market, which operated there for more than 90 years until 2008. A subsequent tenant occupied the combined space from 2014 to 2024 and reported unresolved problems with electricity, flooring and water damage, and a wall that was added to the space and then removed within months. In September 2026 a plan to open a bakery in the space fell through once the zoning split — which would require new exits and a sprinkler system to legally resolve — came to light. Individuals named in the story, on both sides of the dispute, are not recorded here, nor is the property's owner.

extra.renovation_required: new exits and a sprinkler system to legally combine the units

citation.label: The San Francisco Standard, “A former tenant, a dream bakery, and a warning that came too late,” 26 September 2026

raw.text: The 1,800-square-foot space is, legally, two separate units, she explained. Part is zoned for commercial use, but two-thirds is zoned as residential.
